top.title: Agent Cloud Startup Daytona Hits $1B Valuation Backed by FirstMark and a Who's Who of Angels
top.summary: Daytona, a cloud platform for AI agents, has reached $1B valuation with backing from founders of Stripe, Perplexity, Datadog, and others. The startup aims to provide isolated compute environments for autonomous agents.
top.relevance: Signals strong venture market confidence in agentic AI infrastructure and highlights emerging ecosystem players that will reshape enterprise data and analytics architectures—important for monitoring technology trends and competitive positioning.

top.title: Agentic Analytics: Building a Data Foundation for AI Agents
top.summary: Snowflake details how agentic analytics enables AI agents to investigate business questions autonomously and how companies can ground, run, and govern that work. The platform approach combines data infrastructure with agent governance and orchestration.
top.relevance: Offers practical architectural insights into how to operationalize agentic AI at scale—essential knowledge for data and analytics leaders designing systems that allow autonomous AI agents to work safely and effectively in enterprise environments.

top.title: Designing an AI Serving Harness Built to Last
top.summary: MIT Technology Review argues the next competitive advantage in enterprise AI centers not on model selection but on the infrastructure, governance, and operational systems built around the model. The shift marks a maturation of the AI industry.
top.relevance: Validates a critical strategic insight: competitive differentiation is moving from models to platforms and operating models—reshaping how analytics and AI consultants should position value and where clients should focus investment.

top.title: Making the Case for Context-Aware AI
top.summary: MIT Technology Review explores how enterprise AI systems can embed business context—constraints, relationships, and decision-making logic—to generate more accurate recommendations and decisions. Without context, even powerful models miss critical factors.
top.relevance: Highlights why generic AI models underperform in enterprises and why domain expertise, business process knowledge, and data strategy remain central to AI value creation—a key differentiator for specialized consulting firms.

top.title: AI's Hidden Storage Bill: What Inference Leaves Behind
top.summary: MIT Technology Review reveals that data storage costs—often invisible in AI cost analyses—represent a significant ongoing expense for AI systems. Organizations must account for all data generated and retained from model inference and operations.
top.relevance: Essential insight for financial planning and business case development: AI total cost of ownership extends well beyond compute and must include persistent storage for governance, audit, and compliance—a hidden cost that reshapes ROI analysis.

top.title: The Formula for Agentic AI Value
top.summary: BCG's 2026 Applied AI Index shows half of companies now generate value from AI, with top performers seeing 2.5x shareholder returns. The analysis identifies agentic AI as the next frontier, projected to represent 39% of total AI value by 2030.
top.relevance: Provides empirical evidence on what separates AI winners from laggards and charts the shift toward agentic systems—critical strategic input for advising clients on transformation priorities and competitive positioning.

top.title: Horizon Context: Put Business Knowledge to Work for AI
top.summary: Snowflake's Horizon Context, now in public preview with 18 metadata connectors, enables steward permissions and description propagation to ground AI systems in business context. The feature addresses a core challenge in enterprise AI deployment.
top.relevance: Solves a critical pain point in AI deployment: ensuring AI systems have access to accurate business context and governance controls. This is foundational for analytics leaders building trustworthy, auditable AI systems.

top.title: IT Budgets Grow in 2026 as AI Spending Takes Priority
top.summary: BCG reports high-maturity AI adopters rose 10.8 points since mid-2025, with 66% of firms increasing AI and ML spending. Weighted-average ROI on GenAI and AI agent deployments has risen to 13.8%, up from 11.2% six months prior.
top.relevance: Shows emerging proof of ROI from disciplined AI execution and reveals budget reallocation away from legacy tech—critical market intelligence for positioning AI transformation services and understanding where client capital is flowing.

top.title: The AI Operating System: A New Way for CEOs to Run the Enterprise
top.summary: McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey reveals 40% of large companies are scaling AI agents, yet only 6% report significant AI-driven financial impact. The analysis addresses the critical gap between AI adoption rates and actual enterprise value creation.
top.relevance: Directly addresses the ROI challenge that dominates executive conversations: most organizations are investing heavily in AI agents but failing to capture measurable returns, a core concern for consulting leaders advising transformation strategies.

top.title: The State of AI: Global Survey 2026
top.summary: McKinsey's latest global survey documents that 88% of organizations now use AI in at least one function, but only 7% have scaled it across the enterprise. Eight in ten employees report AI has improved personal productivity, yet enterprise-level financial impact remains flat.
top.relevance: Establishes the market landscape showing massive adoption but limited impact—essential baseline data for analytics leaders structuring client engagements and demonstrating why strategic discipline matters more than technology access.

ai.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users (Part II)
ai.summary: OpenAI shares technical architecture for scaling storage to serve billion-user scale, achieving 12x faster reads through multi-tenancy, global caching, and Azure Cosmos DB. Details practical infrastructure patterns.
ai.relevance: For analytics platform leaders scaling systems—provides vendor insight into production patterns for building globally distributed, multi-tenant analytics infrastructure at massive scale.

ai.title: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
ai.summary: The next competitive advantage in enterprise AI comes less from model choice than from the infrastructure and systems built around models. This shift reflects maturation beyond pure capability toward operational excellence.
ai.relevance: Critical for data and analytics leaders planning enterprise AI architecture—emphasizes that sustainable competitive advantage requires robust serving infrastructure, not just frontier models.

ai.title: Making the case for context-aware AI
ai.summary: Enterprise AI systems must understand organizational constraints and relationships to make sound decisions. Context-awareness separates powerful models that miss business realities from those that deliver value.
ai.relevance: Directly relevant to analytics strategy—demonstrates why embedding domain knowledge and business logic into AI systems is essential for enterprise decision-making applications.

ai.title: The Foundations of Scalable AI
ai.summary: Scalable AI requires convergence of data, engineering, platforms, operating models, and governance. This session from MIT EmTech Future conference explores building foundations in highly regulated environments.
ai.relevance: Essential framework for analytics leaders managing enterprise AI governance and operations—addresses the critical need for integrated data, engineering, and compliance infrastructure.

ai.title: AI's hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
ai.summary: Enterprise AI costs extend far beyond GPU compute to include data storage costs from model inference. Most executives overlook this hidden cost component in their AI investment planning.
ai.relevance: Critical for analytics budget planning—reveals often-overlooked storage costs of AI inference that significantly impact total cost of ownership and enterprise AI ROI calculations.

ai.title: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
ai.summary: OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research deployed distributed AI agents to analyze millions of brain cells and uncover research leads. Demonstrates scaled agentic AI applied to complex analytical problems.
ai.relevance: Case study of agentic AI applied to advanced analytics and discovery—shows practical implementation of multi-agent systems for mining insights from massive, unstructured datasets in regulated environments.

ai.title: State of AI in 2026: On the road to ROI
ai.summary: McKinsey's latest global survey shows 40 percent of large enterprises scaling AI agents, with agentic coding tools deployed at scale. Most organizations now deepening AI use across multiple business functions while grappling with infrastructure costs.
ai.relevance: Authoritative benchmark for enterprise AI adoption maturity—demonstrates that agentic AI is moving from pilot to scaled production at large enterprises, with clear patterns around where value concentrates.

ai.title: State of AI trust in 2026: Shifting to the agentic era
ai.summary: As AI systems gain autonomy and interact with other systems, trust and responsible AI practices become foundational requirements. McKinsey survey examines how organizations are approaching trust maturity as agentic systems scale.
ai.relevance: Essential for analytics and AI planning leaders building governance frameworks—shows that responsible AI practices and trust maturity are prerequisites for autonomous agent deployment, not afterthoughts.

ai.title: Reimagining the value proposition of tech services for agentic AI
ai.summary: Enterprise customers are making significant agentic AI investments, with 80 percent of surveyed C-suite executives running pilots and some in scaled deployment. This is driving IT spending increases and reshaping tech services value.
ai.relevance: Key finding for consulting strategy—shows that enterprise agentic AI adoption is accelerating rapidly, with C-suite commitment, indicating strong demand for implementation support and change management.

ai.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
ai.summary: McKinsey's November 2025 survey shows 62 percent of organizations experimenting with AI agents but only 23 percent scaling, with most still in pilot phases. Identifies the pilot-to-production gap as the primary challenge.
ai.relevance: Benchmark for enterprise AI maturity and the critical scaling challenge—establishes that the largest gap in enterprise AI adoption is between pilot-stage curiosity (62%) and scaled production (23%).

platforms.title: Agentic Analytics: Building a Data Foundation for AI Agents
platforms.summary: Snowflake's blog details how its platform grounds, runs, and governs agentic analytics — AI agents that autonomously investigate business questions on enterprise data. The post describes how Horizon Context, Cortex AI, and governance controls combine to enable agents to operate reliably on production data.
platforms.relevance: As clients shift from AI pilots to autonomous agent deployments, understanding Snowflake's native agentic data foundation is essential for consultants advising on data architecture and AI operating model design.

platforms.title: Advancing Digital Sovereignty with Greater Control and Choice
platforms.summary: Microsoft published a senior-leadership post articulating its digital sovereignty strategy for government, critical infrastructure, and regulated industries, emphasizing workload-level control from edge to cloud. The post arrives alongside Snowflake's simultaneous sovereign-cloud announcements with Orange Business and Bleu for France's regulated markets, marking a broader industry-wide push on data residency and sovereign AI.
platforms.relevance: Digital sovereignty is rapidly becoming a board-level requirement in regulated sectors — this Microsoft position paper, read alongside Snowflake's French sovereign-cloud deals, equips consultants to advise clients on compliant multi-cloud AI architectures.

platforms.title: Databricks Acquisition Spree: Panther Labs, Electric, Row Zero and the Lakebase Build-Out
platforms.summary: In 2026 Databricks acquired Panther Labs (AI security operations), Electric (WASM Postgres for AI agent sandboxes), and Row Zero (spreadsheet startup), while expanding Lakebase, its serverless operational database built on the earlier Neon acquisition. AI product revenue reached a $1.7 billion annualized run-rate by June 2026, and data warehousing crossed $1.5 billion ARR, signaling rapid expansion beyond its Spark analytics roots.
platforms.relevance: The acquisition pattern shows Databricks systematically closing the gap with Snowflake on SQL/warehousing and with hyperscalers on security, making platform-selection and build-vs-buy advice for clients increasingly complex.

platforms.title: Snowflake Q2 FY2027 Earnings: Product Revenue Jumps 37% to $1.49B, Full-Year Outlook Raised to $6.07B
platforms.summary: Snowflake posted product revenue of $1.49 billion in Q2 FY2027, up 37% year-over-year — a third consecutive quarter of accelerating growth — and raised its full-year revenue outlook to $6.07 billion. Management credited roughly half the acceleration to its expanding AI portfolio including Cortex Code and CoWork, with the remainder driven by core platform strength and a faster migration pipeline.
platforms.relevance: Accelerating revenue growth and a raised full-year outlook validate Snowflake's agentic-AI platform pivot, a signal that enterprise AI workloads are moving from experimentation to production spending at scale.

platforms.title: Databricks Wraps $5 Billion Funding Round at $190 Billion Valuation
platforms.summary: Databricks closed a $5 billion strategic funding round at a $190 billion valuation, led by Coatue, Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price, and new investor Sixth Street Growth — six months after a prior $5 billion round at a $134 billion valuation. CEO Ali Ghodsi confirmed the company crossed a $7 billion revenue run-rate with more than 80% year-over-year growth and said an IPO remains a future goal but not an immediate priority.
platforms.relevance: A $190 billion private valuation and 80%-plus revenue growth confirm Databricks as the dominant independent data-and-AI platform, raising the competitive stakes for every enterprise platform decision and consulting engagement.

platforms.title: FabCon and SQLCon 2026: Microsoft Unifies Databases and Fabric on a Single Converged Data Platform
platforms.summary: Microsoft announced at FabCon and SQLCon 2026 that it is converging transactional, operational, and analytical data under a single Fabric architecture, powered by Fabric IQ and Power BI semantic models as the AI knowledge layer. New mirroring support was added for Oracle, SAP Datasphere, SharePoint, and Dremio, broadening the platform's ingestion reach significantly.
platforms.relevance: The convergence of SQL Server and Fabric into one architecture is a landmark platform decision that directly affects how consulting teams should recommend data estate modernization roadmaps for Microsoft-heavy enterprise clients.

platforms.title: Snowflake Summit 2026: Context Layer, Custom Model Training via Cortex Training, and Iceberg V3
platforms.summary: Constellation Research analyst coverage of Snowflake Summit 26 highlights three strategic bets: Horizon Context as a business-knowledge layer for AI, Cortex Training enabling enterprises to fine-tune open-weight LLMs on managed GPUs inside Snowflake, and Iceberg V3 deepening open-format data interoperability. Snowflake also raised its FY2027 growth target to 31% on the Q1 earnings call.
platforms.relevance: Third-party analyst synthesis of Snowflake's Summit announcements provides consultants an independent lens on whether Snowflake's agentic and training capabilities represent genuine differentiation or catching up to Databricks.

platforms.title: Microsoft Build 2026: GPU-Accelerated Fabric Data Warehouse and Agentic App Foundation Unveiled
platforms.summary: At Microsoft Build 2026, Microsoft unveiled a GPU-accelerated Fabric Data Warehouse, underpinned by the ACM SIGMOD 2026 Best Paper-winning CoddSpeed architecture, designed to deliver query performance fast enough for interactive agentic workflows. Fabric, OneLake, and Azure AI were positioned as an interoperable open-format ecosystem spanning Delta and Iceberg, designed to connect data beyond Microsoft's own stack.
platforms.relevance: Forbes' independent coverage of Build 2026 highlights that GPU acceleration and open-format interoperability are Microsoft's answers to the Databricks-Snowflake performance narrative — intelligence consultants need when advising clients on AI-ready data warehouse strategy.

platforms.title: Snowflake and Anthropic Accelerate Enterprise AI Adoption, Deepen Cortex AI Integration
platforms.summary: At Snowflake Summit 26, Snowflake and Anthropic announced deepened co-innovation across Cortex AI, with Claude powering Cortex Code and Snowflake CoWork, a Claude Marketplace, and security-focused development workflows. The partnership extends Anthropic's December 2025 integration — placing Claude directly inside the Snowflake governance, security, and collaboration environment without requiring customers to move sensitive data.
platforms.relevance: The Snowflake-Anthropic deepening alongside the separate $200 million OpenAI deal signals that Snowflake is positioning Cortex AI as a multi-model control plane, a critical consideration for clients designing governed enterprise AI architectures.

platforms.title: The End of an Azure Data Platforms Era: Why Microsoft Fabric and Databricks Are Now the Reference Architectures
platforms.summary: Practitioner-analyst Adam Marczak documents that in March 2026 Microsoft formally deprecated its Cloud-Scaled Analytics guidance and removed all Data Landing Zone documentation from Microsoft Learn, replacing it with a Unified Data Platform framework centered on Microsoft Fabric. The post argues that new Azure data platforms should be built Fabric-first or Databricks-first, with Azure serving as backbone rather than core.
platforms.relevance: Microsoft's official deprecation of its Cloud-Scaled Analytics reference architecture is a watershed moment for enterprise data strategy, making this analysis essential reading for consultants guiding clients through Azure estate rationalization and Fabric migration decisions.

planning.title: Pigment Raises $250M Series E at $2.3B Valuation to Accelerate Autonomous Planning
planning.summary: Pigment closed a $250M Series E funding round led by Scaleup Europe Fund at a $2.3B valuation, with participation from NVIDIA and existing investors. The capital will accelerate the company's autonomous planning platform and expand its engineering team, particularly around its proprietary Graphite compute engine and AI agents.
planning.relevance: Critical funding milestone for a leading AI-native planning platform directly competing with legacy EPM vendors; signals strong enterprise adoption momentum with 85% of new metrics now created by AI agents.

planning.title: SAP Advances Finance Operations with Embedded Payments, New Consolidation Capabilities, and Expanded AI
planning.summary: SAP announced enhancements to finance operations including embedded payments, expanded consolidation capabilities, and new AI features that help finance teams move from insight to execution while maintaining governance and control.
planning.relevance: Demonstrates SAP's continued evolution of its finance portfolio with AI-driven capabilities for EPM and finance automation, directly relevant to enterprise planning platform strategy.

planning.title: All of the FP&A Software M&As in 2025-2026
planning.summary: Comprehensive review of FP&A software acquisitions showing private equity and strategic buyers betting on AI-native planning tools, unified Office-of-the-CFO platforms, and consolidated regional players. Notable 2026 transactions include Thoma Bravo merger of Hypergene and Stratsys, and SAP acquisition of Dremio and Prior Labs for AI-ready finance data.
planning.relevance: Market consolidation trends and strategic M&A activity define competitive landscape; signals investor confidence in AI-driven planning platforms and highlights data/AI infrastructure as critical.

planning.title: Anaplan Named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Sales Performance Management
planning.summary: Anaplan was recognized as a Leader in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Sales Performance Management with the highest Ability to Execute among evaluated vendors. The company connects revenue performance management to financial, workforce, and supply chain planning on a single AI-driven platform.
planning.relevance: Validates Anaplan's connected planning approach and AI roadmap as it expands beyond traditional FP&A into revenue and supply chain, key competitive differentiator versus fragmented point solutions.

planning.title: SAP Recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud ERP for Finance
planning.summary: SAP was named a Leader in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Cloud ERP for Finance, emphasizing its focus on helping customers simplify core processes while building capabilities in automation and AI.
planning.relevance: Reinforces SAP's competitive positioning in cloud finance systems as it integrates AI and automation; relevant for understanding ERP-adjacent EPM strategy.

planning.title: Best FP&A Software 2026 Ranked by Size
planning.summary: Market analysis ranking FP&A platforms by company size shows Pigment as clear leader for enterprises above $1B revenue, with Oracle Cloud EPM and Anaplan as aging alternatives. For mid-market, Pigment and Aleph lead; under $100M, Aleph, Datarails, and Runway dominate.
planning.relevance: Independent market assessment quantifying Pigment's emergence as disruptive leader in enterprise planning and positioning of incumbent EPM vendors; critical for understanding competitive disruption dynamics.

planning.title: EPM Software Trends 2026: What Gartner's Financial Planning Research Means for FP&A Leaders
planning.summary: Analysis of Gartner's December 2025 Magic Quadrant for Financial Planning Software shows EPM platforms moving from budgeting tools into connected decision environments with emphasis on AI-assisted planning, xP&A, continuous forecasting, and integrated business planning.
planning.relevance: Authoritative market framing showing industry shift toward integrated, continuous, AI-assisted planning; essential context for understanding competitive positioning of all major EPM vendors.

planning.title: Finance Leaders Are Rewriting the Performance Agenda
planning.summary: BCG research on finance transformation shows leaders moving finance closer to business operations, creating central forecasting groups combining controllers and data scientists, and leveraging shared performance views to drive consistency and speed in decision-making.
planning.relevance: Strategic guidance on finance function evolution and operating model redesign that shapes EPM platform requirements; highlights need for integrated forecasting and analytical capabilities.

planning.title: Anaplan Announces Latest AI-Driven Innovations and Applications to Advance Enterprise Decision-Making
planning.summary: Anaplan announced CoModeler, Custom Analyst, Agent Studio, and 12 new purpose-built applications designed to combine AI reasoning with the platform's deterministic planning engine for accurate, traceable calculations and enterprise decision support.
planning.relevance: Major product innovation announcing agentic AI capabilities as centerpiece of Anaplan's roadmap; directly competitive with Pigment's agent-based planning approach and signals industry shift toward AI-native planning.

planning.title: SAP Puts the Autonomous Enterprise to Work
planning.summary: SAP announced Joule Work, Joule Assistants, and the SAP Business AI Platform at SAP Connect, positioning autonomous capabilities across core business functions to turn business AI into trusted outcomes.
planning.relevance: Core messaging around SAP's autonomous enterprise strategy and AI agent deployment; essential for understanding SAP's competitive positioning versus purpose-built AI planning startups like Pigment.

research.title: The Deployment Failure Holding Back Your AI Investments
research.summary: Early 2026 survey of 6,000 senior executives: 69% use AI actively; more than two-thirds use it personally; nine in ten report no measurable productivity or employment impact. Success requires cross-functional deployment, outcome measurement, and role redesign—not siloed adoption.
research.relevance: Critical insight for consulting positioning: enterprises face AI value realization gap; consulting must focus on cross-functional deployment and operating-model transformation, not just technology adoption.

research.title: How AI Is Changing Data Monetization
research.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) enabling AI agents to access enterprise data; grown from launch (Nov 2024) to 20,000+ servers by July 2026. Poses critical decisions for enterprises: what data to expose, how to provide access, and how to price it in agent-driven workflows.
research.relevance: Emerging strategic question for data monetization consulting: MCP standardization creates new business model and API-economy opportunities; drives demand for data strategy and partner ecosystem design engagements.

research.title: Rearchitecting the Data Platform for the AI Era
research.summary: Data platforms built for BI and reporting cannot support AI workloads. Extended warehouse architecture is practical choice for most enterprises, with lakehouse onramp as workloads mature. CIOs building AI-ready architectures gain lasting competitive edge.
research.relevance: Core infrastructure consulting engagement: organizations need guidance on warehouse/lakehouse architecture decisions and sequencing of data platform modernization.

research.title: How AI Is Reshaping the Consulting Industry (2026)
research.summary: McKinsey cutting 10% of staff (3,000-4,000 roles); KPMG cut 400 advisory positions. Billable-hour model broken by AI productivity (30-60% gains); industry shifting toward outcome-based pricing (McKinsey at 25% of fees in 2025). Junior analyst work most disrupted; platforms and productized consulting growing.
research.relevance: Direct insight into consulting-services business model transformation; outcome-based pricing emergence creates new consulting service lines and margin pressures affecting industry strategy.

research.title: The State of Organizations 2026
research.summary: McKinsey's survey of 10,000+ organizations finds AI Pioneers (23% of leaders) are rolling out agentic AI across departments, automating data-intensive tasks while augmenting decision-making. Three tectonic forces reshaping organizations: AI/automation, data analytics, and AI agents creating paradigm shifts in productivity and cost reduction.
research.relevance: Critical baseline for understanding enterprise AI adoption velocity and organizational readiness across functions; directly informs consulting demand for agentic AI implementation and data transformation.

research.title: AI data readiness: The key to scaling impact
research.summary: As companies push AI pilots to scale, data emerges as a constraint. McKinsey emphasizes need for structured and unstructured data convergence into governed, reusable foundations. Platforms must standardize how unstructured content becomes AI-ready, with observability extending to context assembly and output production.
research.relevance: Core consulting opportunity: data readiness is blocking AI value realization; defines scope for data strategy, platform modernization, and AI-native architecture engagements.

research.title: Building the foundations for agentic AI at scale
research.summary: Nearly two-thirds of enterprises have experimented with agents, but fewer than 10 percent have scaled them. Data limitations are the primary roadblock: eight in ten companies cite data constraints as barriers to scaling agentic AI. McKinsey outlines need to agentify workflows, modernize data architectures, enforce data quality, and evolve operating models.
research.relevance: Identifies the critical data-infrastructure gap that drives demand for consulting engagements in data modernization, data governance, and AI-ready transformation.

research.title: Top Trends in Data and Analytics for 2026
research.summary: Leading 2026 trends: AI agents, advancements in semantics, and D&A platform convergence. Agentic data streaming adoption will jump from under 15% (2025) to over 60% by 2028. More than one in ten enterprises will be AI-first by 2030 through these three areas.
research.relevance: Strategic imperative framework for data leaders planning AI transformation; defines consulting focus areas on agents, semantic layers, and platform consolidation.

research.title: The State of AI in the Enterprise 2026
research.summary: Deloitte survey of 3,235 leaders finds worker AI access rose 50% in 2025; companies with ≥40% projects in production to double in six months. One-third undertaking deep transformation; another third redesigning processes; final third at surface level. Success hinges on moving from ambition to activation.
research.relevance: Quantifies AI adoption heterogeneity across enterprises, revealing large cohorts needing process redesign and operating-model transformation consulting.

research.title: The agentic reality check: Preparing for a silicon-based workforce
research.summary: Many agentic AI implementations are failing because organizations automate existing processes designed by humans without reimagining workflows. Leading organizations managing agents as workers are finding success. Requires rethinking operations, not just process automation.
research.relevance: High-priority consulting challenge: organizations need transformation strategy expertise to move beyond automation to reimagined operations for agentic systems.
